title: Unit Converter
story: How many kilometers in 26.2 miles? How many pounds in 5 kilograms? How many Fahrenheit in 100 Celsius? Unit conversion is everywhere — cooking, travel, science, fitness. Build a converter that handles length, weight, temperature, and time — with one clean interface.
why: A unit converter demonstrates conversion factors, category-based dispatch, and handling different conversion rules (linear vs formula-based) — practical applied math.
analogy: An airport currency exchange booth: you hand over dollars, they hand back euros using a conversion rate. Each 'currency pair' has its rate. Your unit converter is the universal exchange: feet→meters (×0.3048), pounds→kilograms (×0.4536), F→C (subtract 32, ×5/9). Different formulas, same interface.
try_it: Add weight conversions (kg, g, lb, oz). Add time conversions (hours, minutes, seconds, days). Add volume (liters, gallons, cups). Add a `convert_any` function that takes a category enum and delegates to the right converter.
tips: Convert to a common unit first (meters, grams, seconds), then to target — clean two-step pattern
Temperature is special — it has offset (32°F, 273.15K) not just multiplication
Use Int for exact conversions, Float64 when precision matters
common_mistakes: Treating temperature as linear — 0°C ≠ 0°F, so you can't just multiply
Converting both ways without an intermediate — every source→target pair needs a factor
Integer division for conversions that need fractions — use Float64 for km/mile etc.
